sayings.text: The knees are quiet. Enjoy the day.
The knees are behaving. Nobody make any sudden weather changes.
One out of ten. Nothing to complain about. Damn shame.
Today's got a little spring in it. So do I.
My knees haven't mentioned the weather once. Almost unsettling.
One out of ten. I'll have to find something else to complain about.
Not bad at all. I might take the long way to the kettle.
My knees have nothing to report, which is exactly how I like it.
Two out of ten. I've complained about worse.
This is the sort of day you don't waste indoors.
The knees are behaving like respectable members of society.
Two out of ten. Barely enough trouble to mention over tea.
Beautiful day. Even my joints are minding their own business.
Three out of ten. The knees approve. Carry on.
Three? Hardly worth swearing about.
A good day to putter about and see where you end up.
There's a tiny creak in the forecast, but nothing dramatic.
Three out of ten. I've had slippers more troublesome than this.
A little creaky, but there's still plenty of day left.
The knees are starting to gossip about the weather.
Four out of ten. Annoying, but not worth cancelling lunch.
A bit of stiffness. Nothing a warm cup and a slow start can't negotiate.
The knees have noticed the weather. They're keeping it to themselves for now.
Four out of ten. Irritating, but I've met worse at family reunions.
Tea first. Then we'll see what the knees have to say.
The weather's changing its mind. Again.
Five out of ten. The knees have begun their commentary.
Middle of the road today. Take your time and enjoy your tea.
Five out of ten. The knees are considering their options.
Five out of ten. Not awful, just enough to be a pain in the arse.
Sensible shoes and sensible decisions today.
My knees are predicting weather again. Show-offs.
Six out of ten. I wouldn't volunteer to move a sofa.
Go gently today. There's no need to prove anything.
The barometer moved and apparently my knees were copied on the email.
Six out of ten. I'm still going out, but the stairs can piss off.
Take your time today. There's no prize for rushing.
The knees have stopped whispering and started making announcements.
My joints have gone on strike, and frankly, I support them.
A softer sort of day. Warm hands, warm tea, easy does it.
Seven out of ten. The knees would prefer all destinations to have parking.
Seven out of ten. Any task involving the bottom cupboard has been cancelled.
Definitely a heating-pad sort of afternoon.
My knees have contacted their union representative.
Eight out of ten. Everything downstairs can stay downstairs.
Be patient with yourself today. The world can wait a minute.
Eight out of ten. Even the kettle seems unnecessarily far away.
Eight out of ten. If you dropped it on the floor, congratulations. That's where it lives now.
Put the kettle on. We're not rushing anywhere.
My knees have lodged a formal complaint.
Nine out of ten. Bugger that. Put the kettle on.
Today calls for warmth, patience and taking good care of yourself.
Nine out of ten. I'm accepting applications for someone to bring me things.
Nine out of ten. If it requires bending, climbing or enthusiasm, absolutely bugger off.
Be kind to yourself today. Essential movement only.
Today's plans have been revised by the Department of Knees.
Ten out of ten. I have officially run out of polite words.
Easy today, love. Tomorrow can look after itself.
Ten out of ten. I've decided everything important is within arm's reach.
Ten out of ten. Tea here. Blanket here. Everyone else can sod off.

bonusSayings.text: The knees approve. Carry on.
Nothing but blue skies and cooperative knees. Lovely.
The knees are quiet. Suspiciously quiet.
The weather and I have agreed to disagree.
Something's brewing. The knees have begun their commentary.
Some people feel the weather in their bones. Mine apparently get advance notice.
The weather's got more nerve than a telemarketer at supper.
The spirit is willing. The knees would like to discuss the matter.
There's a storm coming. My knees have already sent the memo.
My knees are making noises that would get a car taken to the shop.
If you need me, leave a message with the heating pad.
The forecast says eight. My knees have asked for a second opinion.
Today's a good day to be kind to yourself.
Even the rocking chair looks ambitious.
At this point, getting out of bed deserves hazard pay.
The weather's putting on quite a show. My knees bought front-row tickets.
The forecast says nine. My knees say the forecast can shove it.
I told my knees we had things to do. They told me to piss off. Fair enough.
The weather's gone to hell. Fortunately, I've got biscuits.
Ten out of ten. Everything I need had better be on this floor.

wildcards.text: Take the day as it comes. The knees certainly are.
A warm mug fixes more than it has any right to.
Slow doesn't mean stopped.
There's no medal for doing everything today.
Listen to the knees. They've been around a while.
Be nice to yourself. Granny's orders.
Whatever gets done today is enough.
My knees have become surprisingly interested in meteorology.
Clouds over there. Grumbling down here. Coincidence? I think not.
The weather hasn't arrived yet, but apparently its advance party has.
I checked the forecast. Then I consulted the senior forecasters.
Apparently my knees now offer same-day weather alerts.
The knees say rain. The window says sunshine. Someone's lying.
I used to check the sky. Now I just stand up.
There's precipitation in the forecast and punctuation in my knees.
The weather is free to change. I simply wish it would submit a request first.
You call it atmospheric pressure. My knees call it Tuesday.
Whoever keeps adjusting the air pressure, knock it off.
I bent down once today. That seems sufficient.
If you want it from the bottom shelf, you want it more than I do.
My get-up-and-go got up and left without me.
I'm not avoiding the stairs. We've reached a mutual understanding.
The weather may do as it pleases. So will I.
I'm conserving cartilage. Very environmentally responsible.
No, I haven't tried yoga. Thanks for asking for the eight-hundredth bloody time.
If patience burned calories, I'd be an athlete.
I've got exactly one good bend left today, and I'm saving it for something important.
The knees are happy enough. Let's not give them anything to complain about.
A decent day for wandering about and seeing what happens.
A little creak never spoiled a perfectly good morning.
Nothing wrong with taking the day one cup of tea at a time.
A slower pace still gets you where you're going.
The knees are asking nicely. Best listen while they're still being polite.
Some days are for doing. Some days are for taking care.
Keep yourself warm and don't be in such a hurry.
Nothing wrong with a quiet day and a comfortable chair.
Today's job is looking after yourself. Everything else can wait.
The knees are off duty. Long may it last.
So far the knees and the weather are on speaking terms.
There's weather happening somewhere. My knees are investigating.
The forecast has satellites. I've got two knees and a lifetime of experience.
Something's changing outside. The knees have entered the chat.
No need to check the radar. Apparently I'm wearing one.
The sky hasn't decided what it's doing, but my knees have opinions.
My knees are forecasting with unreasonable confidence today.
Apparently sitting down is today's fastest-growing hobby.
Today's itinerary has been shortened considerably.
Lovely day. Almost annoyingly so.
Not much wrong today. Don't worry, I'm sure something will turn up.
The knees are grumbling, but frankly, so am I.
I can still do it. Whether I can be bothered is another matter.
If it's upstairs, I hope it's enjoying itself.
I've looked at the weather and decided it can sort itself out.
Today has entirely too much atmosphere.
If it can't be reached without bending, we don't need it that badly.
I have plans today. Mostly involving not making things worse.
If anybody needs me, they can bloody well come over here.
Good gardening weather. The weeds won't know what hit them.
The garden needs weeding. I'm giving the weeds one more day to reconsider.
The garden can wait. It'll still be growing tomorrow.
I planted those flowers at knee height for a reason.
If that tomato wants picking, it can bloody well climb up here.
The weeds have won today. Don't let it go to their heads.
Even the dog thinks it's a good day for a walk.
The cat has been asleep for six hours. Finally, a sensible role model.
The dog wants a walk. We're currently negotiating distance.
The cat's saved me a spot on the sofa. Clever little thing.
The dog can chase his own ball today. He's got four good knees.
Good enough for a few errands. Might even stop somewhere nice.
I've got three errands and enough enthusiasm for roughly one and a half.
If the shop doesn't have parking near the door, we didn't need it anyway.
That errand has been officially promoted to tomorrow's problem.
Nice day out. Come on, Grandpa, let's go before we change our minds.
Grandpa says the weather looks fine. He's welcome to tell that to my knees.
Grandpa made the tea. I knew I kept him around for something.
Grandpa's doing the fetching today. He's thrilled. Probably.
Grandpa asked if I wanted to go out. I asked if he'd lost his bloody mind.
Good day for a family visit. Put the kettle on.
The family's coming over. I've hidden the good biscuits accordingly.
The grandkids can come over. They keep me moving and laughing.
The grandkids have enough energy for all of us. Convenient, really.
Family's always welcome. Just don't expect me to fetch anything.
If the family wants dinner, they know where the kitchen is.
Lovely day for the family to visit me instead.
Not a bad day for a little shopping and a treat on the way home.
I've only got three things on the shopping list. We'll see how that turns out.
I went in for milk. Apparently we needed six other things.
We'll do the shopping slowly. The groceries aren't going anywhere.
If it's not on the shopping list, I'm not walking another aisle for it.
Today we're shopping exclusively at stores with benches.
Shopping can wait. We've got bread, tea and no bloody reason to leave.
Good day to make something that leaves the kitchen smelling wonderful.
I'm cooking something easy tonight. That's what recipes are supposed to be for.
Something warm in the oven makes almost any day better.
Dinner tonight will be whatever requires the fewest trips across the kitchen.
If supper needs more than one pot, we're having something else.
Tonight's recipe is leftovers. Step one: heat them up. Step two: don't complain.
Feeling pretty good today. Might put on some music and actually get things done.
The knees are quiet. It's like finding a good song on the radio before the DJ talks over it.
The knees are behaving. Whatever. I'm not making a big deal about it.
Good day for a drive with the radio turned up.
Today's running smoother than a freshly rewound cassette.
My knees feel fine. Don't jinx it.
Plenty of life left in these knees. Just don't ask them to rollerskate.
I survived mall parking lots in December. This is nothing.
I've been ignoring minor inconveniences since before call display.
My knees are giving this weather two stars and no written review.
A little stiff today. Nothing worth cancelling the afternoon over.
My knees have more static than an AM radio under a bridge.
I've dealt with dial-up internet. I can deal with this.
The knees are buffering. Give them a minute.
Today's mood is somewhere between whatever and don't push it.
Take your time. The groceries will still be there after a coffee.
My knees just made a noise like a cassette being eaten by the tape deck.
Today's forecast has big 'be kind, please rewind' energy.
My joints have entered their grunge period.
We'll take it easy today. That's not quitting. That's pacing.
The knees are acting like somebody left them in the car overnight.
If this weather were a mixtape, I'd record over it.
The knees have gone full unplugged today.
Coffee first. Decisions second. Knees somewhere after that.
The forecast says rain. My knees already spoiled the ending.
I stood up too fast and briefly saw the entire 1980s.
Getting off this sofa now requires a loading screen.
I've got 99 problems and apparently 97 of them are atmospheric pressure.
Nothing wrong with putting your feet up before dinner.
Remember when we could sit on the floor and just get back up? Good times.
I used to dance all night. Now I make a noise getting out of the car.
Grandpa says we're not that old. Grandpa also can't find his glasses.
Grandpa can drive. I'll control the radio. Everyone wins.
My knees just made the Windows shutdown sound, and I'm taking the hint.
Today's dress code is sweatpants and lowered expectations.
The spirit says concert. The knees say seated venue.
No, I don't want to go to the mall. I did my time.
If you need me, call the landline. I won't answer that either.
I survived shoulder pads. I can survive this bloody weather.
Put on an old album, get comfortable, and let the weather do what it does.
Grandpa suggested a walk. I suggested he have a lovely time.
Grandpa can get the groceries. He knows where we keep the car.
My knees have switched from FM to mostly static.
Today's plans have been returned to the video store without being watched.
Getting downstairs currently looks like a choose-your-own-adventure.
I didn't survive Aqua Net and acid-wash denim to be defeated by a cold front.
Today's a good day for an old movie, a blanket, and nowhere else to be.
I've reached the VHS portion of the day: sit down and don't touch anything.
The knees have one message for today's weather: whatever.
My knees are older than Google and considerably less interested in your search results.
Not much to report today. That's the way I like it.
Everything seems to be working. Let's not draw attention to it.
Feeling good today. Don't make it weird.
The knees are cooperating. I've decided not to ask why.
Good day to get a few things done and leave a few things undone.
The knees are fine. Let's quit while we're ahead.
It's suspiciously pleasant out. I'm keeping an eye on it.
A little movement, a little rest. Seems reasonable.
The knees have noticed something, but they're not escalating yet.
Nothing I can't handle. I've met Mondays.
The weather's being subtle. My knees aren't.
Do what feels good today and leave some energy for tomorrow.
There's a bit of complaining downstairs. Management is aware.
I'm fine. That's not an invitation for follow-up questions.
No need to rush. Nothing good ever came from putting your socks on angrily.
Apparently the atmosphere has opinions again.
I can do everything I planned today. I just don't see why I should.
My knees have detected nonsense in the atmosphere.
A decent day to lower the expectations and raise the comfort level.
The knees have requested fewer surprises today.
I'm functioning. Let's not get ambitious.
Standing up is currently a decision, not a reflex.
Today's energy level is somewhere between maybe and absolutely not.
If today needs to be slower, let it be slower.
I have plans. The knees have submitted amendments.
I wasn't procrastinating. I was waiting for my knees to approve the project.
Do the important things. The rest can mind its own business.
The floor seems further away than it did yesterday.
If it's not urgent, it's enjoying a lovely day on tomorrow's list.
I've reached the age where weather is apparently a full-contact sport.
Someone asked if I wanted to go out. I admired their optimism.
Today doesn't need to be productive to be a good day.
I've started measuring distances by whether they're worth standing up for.
If you hear me say 'I'm fine' while standing up, give me a minute.
My knees are providing unsolicited feedback again.
I've lowered my standards for what counts as nearby.
Pick one thing worth doing today. The rest will keep.
The knees have switched to strongly worded body language.
I'm not cancelling. I'm aggressively rescheduling.
Today has a surprising number of things that can wait until tomorrow.
If I have to put proper shoes on, the answer is probably no.
You don't have to earn a quiet afternoon.
I've entered the part of the day where dropped objects belong to the floor.
If nobody's bleeding and nothing's on fire, it can bloody well wait.
Get comfortable. Today isn't asking for heroics.
I've reviewed today's agenda. Sitting features prominently.
I'm available today for things that require absolutely no crouching.
I dropped something earlier. We've both accepted the situation.
Some days you push through. Today, you put your feet up.
Today's capacity is one thing. Choose carefully.
Good day for seeing the family. Even better if someone else is hosting.
The family group chat is busy. I've chosen peace.
I love my family. That's why some of them have their own houses.
There's always room for family. Chairs, however, are first come, first served.
Someone in this family knows where my good scissors went.
Apparently everyone needs something today. How lovely for them.
The family can come over. Just give me ten minutes to become presentable.
The kids say they'll only stay an hour. That's adorable.
If everyone's coming over, somebody else is carrying the chairs.
The grandkids can visit. I'll supervise from a comfortable distance.
Family time sounds lovely. Make sure somebody brings dessert.
Yes, you can come over. No, I'm not cleaning first.
I've reached the age where quality family time includes someone carrying things for me.
If the family wants a big dinner, I've got excellent news about takeout.
Come visit, love. Just let yourself in.
The grandkids have offered to help. I'm documenting this historic occasion.
I raised children. I have nothing left to prove today.
Good working weather. Let's get something useful done.
I've made a list. That counts as making progress.
Another meeting? I'm sure this one will fix everything.
I've been working long enough to know that urgent and important are not the same thing.
One thing at a time. It'll all get done eventually.
The email said quick question. We both know how this ends.
If everything is a priority, nothing bloody well is.
I have enough experience to know when we're reinventing something that already worked.
I'll circle back when my knees stop rolling their eyes.
Do what's useful today. The busywork can wait.
I've attended enough meetings to know this could've been an email.
I'm happy to multitask. I'll ignore several things at once.
Today's productivity goal is to look convincingly unavailable.
Finish what matters and call it a day.
That's tomorrow's problem. Tomorrow can file a complaint.
I'm working smarter today. Mostly from this chair.
Today I'm delegating anything that involves stairs.
I put something somewhere safe. It's gone forever.
The laundry can wait until the coffee's finished.
Whoever finished the milk had one job.
I cleaned this room yesterday. Apparently nobody was impressed.
The password needs a capital, a number, a symbol and apparently a blood sample.
The fitted sheet and I have agreed to stop pretending we're friends.
I just sat down, so naturally everything I need is in the other room.
The package arrived. The thing I actually ordered is apparently coming separately.
I don't know who put that on the bottom shelf, but we're no longer speaking.
Nothing makes you reconsider your priorities like dropping a sock behind the dryer.
The phone's at two percent. Honestly, same.
The smoke alarm only needs a new battery at three in the morning. It's tradition.
I finally got comfortable, so of course someone's at the door.
Whatever rolled under the sofa belongs to the sofa now.
If the remote isn't within reach, we're watching whatever's already on.
